title: Acute encephalitis syndrome (AES) and Japanese encephalitis
subject: infectious-disease
summary: Fever of up to 5 to 7 days with altered sensorium or new seizures. Stabilise airway, breathing and circulation, correct hypoglycaemia, control seizures and raised ICP, and start empirical ceftriaxone, acyclovir, doxycycline (scrub typhus) and artesunate if malaria is not excluded, then narrow by results.

sections.title: Recognise (case definition)
items: AES (MoHFW/WHO): acute onset of fever of not more than 5 to 7 days, with a change in mental status (confusion, disorientation, coma, inability to talk) and/or new onset of seizures, excluding simple febrile seizures.

Common causes in India: Japanese encephalitis, scrub typhus, HSV, enteroviruses, dengue, Chandipura, Nipah (Kerala), cerebral malaria, bacterial or tuberculous meningitis, sepsis-associated encephalopathy, and litchi-associated hypoglycaemic encephalopathy (Muzaffarpur).
Non-infective mimics: ADEM, autoimmune (anti-NMDA receptor) encephalitis, Reye syndrome, toxins and drugs, metabolic encephalopathy, non-convulsive status epilepticus.

Pointers: JE (endemic district, dystonia or extrapyramidal signs, thalamic and basal ganglia change on MRI; a rash argues against JE); HSV (focal seizures, temporal lobe change, PLEDs on EEG); scrub typhus (eschar, thrombocytopenia, raised transaminases); malaria (symmetrical signs, pallor, splenomegaly).

sections.title: First hour
items: Airway: intubate if GCS below 8, impaired airway reflexes, abnormal breathing pattern, signs of raised ICP or herniation, SpO2 below 92% despite high-flow oxygen, or fluid-refractory shock.

Circulation: IV access, bloods (glucose, CBC, electrolytes, renal and liver function, gas, lactate, blood culture, malaria smear and RDT); 20 mL/kg 0.9% saline bolus for circulatory failure, then inotropes if needed.

Check glucose at once. Hypoglycaemia: children 10% dextrose 2 mL/kg (200 mg/kg), adults 100 mL of 25% dextrose with thiamine 100 mg IV; then dextrose-containing fluids. In litchi-season AES in Bihar, early dextrose is life-saving.

Seizures: IV lorazepam 0.1 mg/kg or midazolam 0.2 mg/kg or diazepam 0.3 mg/kg (no IV: IM, buccal or intranasal midazolam 0.2 mg/kg), then phenytoin 20 mg/kg IV (no faster than 1 mg/kg/min, maximum 50 mg/min).
Refractory seizures: ICU and midazolam infusion; if ICU is unavailable, valproate 20 mg/kg, levetiracetam 20 to 40 mg/kg or phenobarbitone 20 mg/kg IV.
Treat fever with paracetamol and sponging; nurse head end up 15 to 30 degrees; nil by mouth with nasogastric drainage while obtunded.

sections.title: Empirical antimicrobials (start immediately after blood cultures)
items: Ceftriaxone: children 100 mg/kg/day IV in 2 divided doses (maximum 4 g/day); adults 2 g IV 12-hourly. Continue 10 to 14 days if bacterial meningitis is confirmed. Adults over 50 or immunocompromised: add ampicillin 2 g IV 4-hourly.

Acyclovir for all sporadic suspected viral encephalitis: 3 months to 12 years 500 mg/m2 IV 8-hourly; over 12 years and adults 10 mg/kg IV over 1 hour 8-hourly. Maintain hydration and adjust for renal function.

Stop acyclovir if another diagnosis is confirmed, or if CSF HSV PCR is negative on two samples 24 to 48 hours apart with an MRI not suggesting HSV. Confirmed HSV: 14 to 21 days (at least 21 days in children 3 months to 12 years).

Doxycycline for possible scrub typhus (a major cause of AES in Gorakhpur and other endemic areas): adults 100 mg 12-hourly; children 2.2 mg/kg 12-hourly (maximum 100 mg), orally or by nasogastric tube if IV is unavailable; or azithromycin 10 mg/kg/day (adults 500 mg/day).
Artesunate until malaria is excluded: 2.4 mg/kg IV (3 mg/kg if under 20 kg) at 0, 12 and 24 hours, then daily; stop if both smear and RDT are negative.

sections.title: Investigations
items: CT or MRI before lumbar puncture if papilloedema, platelets below 50,000, focal deficits, asymmetric or unreactive pupils, or decerebrate or decorticate posturing. MRI is preferred.
CSF: cells, protein, glucose (with paired blood glucose), Gram stain, culture, AFB and GeneXpert, HSV PCR, JE IgM (MAC-ELISA), and store 10 mL for further tests.
Serum JE IgM, scrub typhus IgM, dengue NS1 and IgM, leptospira serology, HIV; blood and urine cultures; chest X-ray; EEG where available.
Laboratory-confirmed JE: IgM in serum and/or CSF, fourfold IgG rise in paired sera, virus isolation, antigen or PCR detection. Send samples to the sentinel surveillance laboratory.

sections.title: Raised intracranial pressure and supportive care
items: Mannitol 0.25 g/kg IV bolus, then 0.25 g/kg 6-hourly as needed for up to 48 hours, after correcting dehydration.
With hypotension, hypovolaemia or renal failure, prefer 3% saline 0.1 to 1 mL/kg/h by infusion, targeting serum sodium 145 to 155 mmol/L.
Impending herniation: intubate and hyperventilate briefly to PaCO2 30 to 35 mmHg; sedation and analgesia; lignocaine before suctioning.
Steroids are not indicated in viral encephalitis including JE. Give pulse methylprednisolone only for suspected ADEM or autoimmune encephalitis.
Maintain euglycaemia, hydration and nutrition (early nasogastric feeding); eye care, turning to prevent pressure sores, bladder care and physiotherapy.

sections.title: Escalation, reporting and discharge
items: Admit every AES case. Transfer to ICU or PICU with ventilation for GCS below 8, abnormal breathing, fluid-refractory shock, decerebrate or decorticate posturing, or seizures persisting despite a benzodiazepine and phenytoin.
AES is notifiable: report every case through IDSP and send JE samples to the sentinel laboratory.

Discharge when haemodynamically stable, afebrile, seizure-free, consciousness improving, feeding orally, and the family is trained in home care and physiotherapy; arrange neurodevelopmental follow-up.

sections.title: Prevention
items: JE vaccine in the Universal Immunization Programme in endemic districts: 2 doses, at 9 months (with measles-rubella) and at 16 to 24 months (with DPT booster).
Adult JE vaccination campaigns are run in selected high-burden districts; check the state programme.
Vector control, mosquito nets and repellents, and keeping pigs away from dwellings in JE areas.
Litchi-growing areas: children should eat an evening meal and should not eat litchis on an empty stomach; treat any drowsy child for hypoglycaemia at once.

sections.title: Pitfalls
items: Delaying acyclovir while waiting for CSF or MRI.
Missing hypoglycaemia, cerebral malaria or scrub typhus, all of which are rapidly treatable.
Lumbar puncture in a patient with signs of raised ICP or severe thrombocytopenia.
Labelling every case JE; most AES in several endemic districts has another, treatable cause.
Giving steroids routinely for JE.

drugs.name: Ceftriaxone
drugs.dose: Children 100 mg/kg/day IV in 2 divided doses (maximum 4 g/day); adults 2 g IV 12-hourly
drugs.notes: Empirical cover for bacterial meningitis; 10 to 14 days if confirmed.

drugs.name: Acyclovir
drugs.dose: 3 months to 12 years 500 mg/m2 IV 8-hourly; over 12 years and adults 10 mg/kg IV over 1 hour 8-hourly
drugs.notes: 14 to 21 days if HSV confirmed. Hydrate; reduce dose in renal impairment.

drugs.name: Doxycycline
drugs.dose: Adults 100 mg 12-hourly; children 2.2 mg/kg 12-hourly (maximum 100 mg per dose)
drugs.notes: Empirical scrub typhus cover; 7 days if confirmed.

drugs.name: Azithromycin
drugs.dose: Children 10 mg/kg once daily; adults 500 mg once daily
drugs.notes: Alternative scrub typhus cover, including pregnancy.

drugs.name: Artesunate
drugs.dose: 2.4 mg/kg IV (3 mg/kg under 20 kg) at 0, 12 and 24 hours, then daily
drugs.notes: Until malaria excluded; if positive, complete with full oral ACT.

drugs.name: Mannitol 20%
drugs.dose: 0.25 g/kg IV bolus, then 0.25 g/kg 6-hourly as needed, up to 48 hours

drugs.name: Hypertonic saline 3%
drugs.dose: 0.1 to 1 mL/kg/h IV infusion, target sodium 145 to 155 mmol/L
drugs.notes: Preferred over mannitol with hypotension, hypovolaemia or renal failure.

drugs.name: Lorazepam or midazolam
drugs.dose: Lorazepam 0.1 mg/kg IV; midazolam 0.2 mg/kg IV, IM, buccal or intranasal

drugs.name: Phenytoin
drugs.dose: 20 mg/kg IV loading, no faster than 1 mg/kg/min (maximum 50 mg/min)

drugs.name: Dextrose
drugs.dose: Children 10% dextrose 2 mL/kg IV; adults 100 mL of 25% dextrose IV with thiamine 100 mg
drugs.notes: Treat hypoglycaemia immediately, then dextrose-containing maintenance fluid.
